mainTopic: Can one person's small amount of property (water and salt borrowed for dough) be nullified (בטל) inside another person's larger property, for the laws of תחומין on יום טוב?
overview: The משנה rules that if a woman borrows water and salt from her friend for her dough, the dough may only go where both women may walk. Why aren't the water and salt simply בטל in the dough? רבי אבא argued that one person's property is never nullified into someone else's, using wheat mixed with wheat as his example, and the Sages laughed at him. רב אושעיא explained the laughter: according to the רבנן, wheat in wheat is בטל. רב ספרא defended רבי אבא from רב's ruling that one who removes pebbles from his friend's grain must pay for them as wheat. אביי answered that property with an active claimant is different from property with none. רב ספרא pushed back with רב חסדא's rule about נבלה and שחוטה and with רבי יוחנן בן נורי's teaching that ownerless objects acquire שביתה. אביי replied that איסור and ממון follow different rules: an איסור can be בטל, but money cannot. So the גמרא asks for the real reason. אביי says it is a גזירה because of dough made in partnership, and רבא says salt is added for taste, and taste is never בטל.

steps.title: רבי אבא's wheat example
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא argues that one person's property cannot be nullified into another's. If one קב of my wheat mixed into ten קבין of my friend's wheat, should my friend just eat it all and be happy?
steps.simpleTranslation: If one person's single קב of wheat got mixed into ten קבין of his friend's wheat, should the friend eat it all and rejoice?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא is giving the Sages an example to prove his point. He wants to show why the borrowed water and salt are not nullified in the dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that ownership is not lost just because a small amount is mixed into a large amount. Nobody would agree that the owner of ten קבין now owns all eleven. In the same way, the lender's water and salt still belong to her, so the dough is limited by her תחום too.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of volume (about the size of 24 eggs)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of רבי אבא's speech. The real topic is the water and salt that a woman borrowed for her dough in the משנה. The wheat is only an example.

phrases.english: Suppose one kav of his wheat became mixed
phrases.notes: A small amount belonging to one person

phrases.english: into ten kav of his friend's wheat,
phrases.notes: A large amount belonging to someone else

phrases.english: shall that other one eat it all and rejoice?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: obviously not

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אבא's statement from the previous part of the daf about the water and salt in the dough.
steps.raayaObject: Borrowed water and salt are not nullified in another person's dough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A logical comparison: one person's wheat does not become another person's just because it mixed into a larger pile.

steps.title: The Sages laugh at רבי אבא
steps.stepSummary: The Sages laugh at רבי אבא's example. He asks if he stole their cloaks, and they laugh at him again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at him. He said to them: Did I take your cloaks? They laughed at him again.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages reject רבי אבא's example by laughing at it. He protests, and they laugh again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laughter shows that the Sages thought the example was weak. רבי אבא's reply means: I did nothing wrong to you, so why embarrass me? The גמרא does not say yet why they laughed. That explanation comes in the next step.

phrases.english: They laughed at him.
phrases.notes: The Sages mocked his example

phrases.english: He said to them: Did I take your cloaks?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why are you shaming me?

phrases.english: They laughed at him again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The Sages' reaction to רבי אבא's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אבא's wheat example as a valid proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated here. רב אושעיא explains it in the next steps.

steps.title: רב אושעיא explains why they laughed: why not wheat in barley?
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא says the Sages were right to laugh. He asks why רבי אבא chose wheat mixed with wheat instead of wheat mixed with barley. The answer is that a different type mixed with another type is clearly בטל, even when the foods belong to two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: They did well to laugh at him. Why didn't he give them the case of wheat mixed with barley? Because that is one type mixed with a different type, and one type mixed with a different type is nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא begins defending the Sages. He points out that רבי אבא avoided the example of wheat in barley, because there everyone agrees the small amount is nullified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מין בשאינו מינו (a type mixed with a different type) is בטל according to everyone, even when two owners are involved. So רבי אבא's claim that ownership blocks ביטול is already shown to be wrong. That is why he had to choose a same-type example, wheat in wheat. The next step shows why that example fails too.

keyTerms.meaning: A type mixed with a different type

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
phrases.notes: Attribution

phrases.english: They did well to laugh at him.
What is different about wheat in barley
phrases.notes: Why did he avoid this example?

phrases.english: that he did not say that to them?
Because it is a type with what is not its type,
and a type with what is not its type is nullified.
phrases.notes: Even when it belongs to someone else

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: שַׁפִּיר עֲבוּד דְּאַחִיכוּ עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the Sages' laughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A food mixed into a different type of food is nullified, even across owners. So ownership alone does not stop ביטול.

steps.title: Wheat in wheat is also nullified according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא finishes his argument. Wheat mixed with wheat is also בטל according to the רבנן. Only רבי יהודה holds that same-type mixtures are not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wheat in wheat too: even though according to רבי יהודה it is not nullified, according to the רבנן it is certainly nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא knocks down רבי אבא's chosen example. He shows that it only works according to רבי יהודה, not according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds מין במינו לא בטל (same type is not nullified). That is a rule about mixtures, not about ownership. According to the רבנן, the single קב would be nullified, so רבי אבא's example proves nothing about ownership. That is why the Sages laughed.

keyTerms.meaning: A type mixed with its own type

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אושעיא, ownership does not stop ביטול. Only רבי יהודה's special rule about same-type mixtures would prevent it.

phrases.english: Wheat in wheat as well:
phrases.notes: רבי אבא's actual example

phrases.english: granted that according to Rabbi Yehuda it is not nullified,
phrases.notes: Same type is not nullified, according to him

phrases.english: according to the Rabbis it is certainly nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the logic of step 3 to רבי אבא's actual wheat-in-wheat case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אבא's proof from wheat mixed with wheat.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The example depends on רבי יהודה's view about same-type mixtures. According to the רבנן it would be nullified, so it shows nothing about ownership.

steps.title: רב ספרא challenges רב אושעיא with a ruling about pebbles
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks רב אושעיא whether he is really right. He cites רב's ruling that someone who removes pebbles from his friend's grain pile must pay him the price of wheat for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to him: משה! Are you speaking correctly?! Didn't they hear what רבי חייא קטוספאה said in the name of רב: One who removes pebbles from his friend's threshing floor must pay him the value of wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא pushes back against רב אושעיא and defends רבי אבא. He brings a ruling of רב about pebbles in grain to set up his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seller can sell grain with some pebbles mixed in at the full wheat price. So removing them causes the owner a real loss. רב makes the one who removed them pay for them as if they were wheat. This means the pebbles were not treated as nullified and gone. The next step spells out what this proves.

keyTerms.meaning: 'משה!', a title of respect for a great scholar

steps.confusionAlert: 'משה!' is not someone's name here. It is a respectful title for רב אושעיא, even while רב ספרא challenges him.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to him:
phrases.notes: Speaking to Rav Oshaya

phrases.english: Moshe! Are you speaking well?!
phrases.notes: A respectful address joined to a challenge

phrases.english: Did they not hear
phrases.notes: The Sages who laughed

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא קְטוֹסְפָאָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: that which Rabbi Chiyya of Ketosfa said in the name of Rav:
One who removes pebbles from his friend's threshing floor
must pay him the value of wheat.
phrases.notes: The pebbles would have been sold along with the wheat

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא: מֹשֶׁה! שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אושעיא's defense of the Sages and returns to support רבי אבא's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אושעיא's claim that the Sages were right to laugh at רבי אבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's ruling shows that a small mixed-in item belonging to an owner is not ignored as nullified. So the Sages should not have laughed.

steps.title: The conclusion: he reduced the owner's measure
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא draws the lesson: removing the pebbles 'reduced the measure' of the grain. In the same way, the borrowed water and salt add to the dough's measure and are not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that he reduced his measure. Here too, he reduced his measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא completes his proof. Since even pebbles count toward the owner's measure, the lender's water and salt also count and are not nullified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If worthless pebbles are not considered nullified in the grain, then water and salt, which have real value, are surely not nullified in the dough. So the dough still carries the lender's share and follows both women's תחום. This supports רבי אבא's point.
steps.whatToRemember: This is רב ספרא's argument: pebbles in grain still count toward the owner's 'measure' (כילא), so the borrowed water and salt should count too. אביי challenges this proof in the next step, and in Step 11 he shows that a monetary case cannot decide a question of איסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רב ספרא's attempt to ground the משנה's ruling in ownership and 'measure'. The גמרא does not end up accepting it: אביי answers that money cases prove nothing about איסור, and the final reasons are a גזירה (אביי) or that taste is not בטל (רבא).

phrases.english: Evidently: he reduced his measure.
phrases.notes: The pebbles were part of the sellable amount

phrases.english: Here too: he reduced his measure.
phrases.notes: Applied to the water and salt in the dough

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from רב's pebble ruling and applies it to the dough.
steps.raayaObject: Borrowed water and salt are not nullified in the dough, so the Sages should not have laughed at רבי אבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that one who removes pebbles from his friend's grain pays the value of wheat.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ספרא's inference: a small addition that is part of the owner's measure is not nullified. This proof is later rejected by אביי (Steps 7 and 11).

steps.title: אביי distinguishes between property that has claimants and property that does not
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב ספרא's proof from the pebbles. That owner is actively claiming his loss, but the lender of water and salt is not asking for anything back right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Doesn't the master see a difference between money that has someone claiming it and money that has no one claiming it?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב ספרא's proof from רב's ruling about the pebbles. He says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pebbles case, the grain owner is demanding payment, so his loss is 'alive' and can't be ignored. The lender of water and salt is not demanding anything now. So maybe those items can be בטל in the dough. If this distinction holds, רב ספרא's proof collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the master see a difference?

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing about the הלכה of the pebbles. He is only saying that case can't serve as proof for the water and salt.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rav Safra):
And does the master not differentiate
between money that has claimants
phrases.notes: Like the grain owner who demands payment for the pebbles.

phrases.english: and money that has no claimants?
phrases.notes: Like the lent water and salt, which no one is demanding back yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof רב ספרא drew in Step 6 from the pebbles case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's comparison between the pebbles and the borrowed water and salt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two cases differ. Property with an active claimant cannot be nullified, but property with no current claimant might be.

steps.title: רב ספרא cites רב חסדא on carcass meat mixed with slaughtered meat
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers with 'according to your logic.' He quotes רב חסדא's rule: נבלה is בטל in שחוטה, but שחוטה is not בטל in נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And according to your reasoning, what about רב חסדא's statement? Carcass meat is nullified in slaughtered meat, because slaughtered meat can never become a carcass. But slaughtered meat is not nullified in carcass meat, because a carcass can become like slaughtered meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא is setting up a counter-attack. He quotes רב חסדא's rule now so that in the next step he can show what it would mean under אביי's distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is explaining רבי יהודה's view that only different types are בטל. שחוטה can never become נבלה, so the two count as different types and the נבלה is בטל. נבלה can lose its טומאה if it rots, so it can become 'like' שחוטה. That makes them the same type, and so the שחוטה is not בטל.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning; a turn-around formula
Meat of an animal that died without proper שחיטה; it is טמא
Meat of a properly slaughtered animal

steps.confusionAlert: 'A נבלה can become שחוטה' does not mean it becomes kosher. It means a rotted נבלה stops transmitting טומאה, so in that respect it is like שחוטה.

phrases.english: He (Rav Safra) said to him: And according to your reasoning,
that which Rav Chisda said:
Carcass meat is nullified in slaughtered meat,
because it is impossible for slaughtered meat
to become a carcass.
phrases.notes: So they count as different types, and nullification works even for רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Slaughtered meat is not nullified in carcass meat,
because it is possible for a carcass
to become like slaughtered meat.
phrases.notes: When it rots, it loses its טומאה. So they count as the same type.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רב ספרא's reply to אביי by bringing in an outside rule to test אביי's distinction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רבי יהודה: נבלה is בטל in שחוטה because they are different types, but שחוטה is not בטל in נבלה because they count as the same type.

steps.title: Would ownership really stop the carcass from being nullified?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא pushes אביי's logic: if the נבלה has an owner, will it suddenly not be בטל? That is absurd.
steps.simpleTranslation: So here too, if the carcass has owners, will it not be nullified?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא delivers the punch of his ולטעמיך. He applies אביי's 'claimants' idea to רב חסדא's case and shows it makes no sense there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ownership and claimants decide nullification, then a נבלה owned by someone else should not be בטל. But nobody thinks רב חסדא's rule depends on who owns the meat. So אביי's distinction seems irrelevant to the laws of ביטול.

keyTerms.meaning: So too; would you really say this?

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּכִי אִית לַהּ בְּעָלִים —
phrases.english: Here too, that when it (the carcass) has owners —
it is not nullified?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּכִי אִית לַהּ בְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies אביי's distinction from Step 7 to רב חסדא's case from Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's distinction between property with claimants and property without.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Ownership has nothing to do with whether a mixture is nullified. Applied to רב חסדא's case, the distinction gives an absurd result.

steps.title: Ownerless objects are treated as if they have owners
steps.stepSummary: Suppose אביי accepts the absurd result. רב ספרא still answers from a ברייתא: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says ownerless objects acquire שביתה as though they had owners. So 'no claimants' does not cancel an item's own status.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: Yes, it really is so — but it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: Ownerless objects acquire שביתה (a שבת resting place). Even though they have no owners, they are treated as if they have owners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא expects אביי might say 'yes, ownership does matter.' He blocks that answer with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי teaches that even items with no owner at all keep their own שביתה, their own שבת limit. If items with no owner still keep their own status, the lent water and salt, which have an owner who just isn't claiming them yet, surely keep their owner's תחום. So lacking an active claimant does not let them be בטל in the dough, and אביי's distinction fails.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; anticipating a reply
But was it not taught in a ברייתא?
Acquire a שבת resting place, which sets their own שבת limit

steps.whatToRemember: אביי suggested that property with no active claimant can be בטל. רב ספרא pushed back twice. First, ownership plainly doesn't matter in רב חסדא's נבלה case. Second, רבי יוחנן בן נורי shows that even ownerless items keep their own status for שביתה. The next step gives אביי's answer: both of these are איסור cases, not monetary ones.
steps.whyThisMatters: This supports the משנה's ruling: borrowed water and salt keep the lender's תחום, even though the lender is not currently claiming them.

phrases.english: And if you say: Indeed, so it is —
but was it not taught in a baraita,
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
Ownerless objects acquire a Shabbat resting place.
phrases.notes: They can be moved only 2,000 אמות from where they were when שבת began.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם בְּעָלִים —
phrases.english: Even though they have no owners —
they are treated as if they have owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי — וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks אביי's possible acceptance of the result in Step 9 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Lacking an active claimant does not remove an item's own שבת status, so the borrowed water and salt are not בטל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוחנן בן נורי: ownerless objects acquire שביתה as though they had owners.

steps.title: You Cannot Compare Prohibition to Money
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב ספרא's proofs because they mix monetary law with איסור law. In איסור a small amount is בטל, but money is never בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you comparing a prohibition to money? A prohibition can be nullified, but money cannot be nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב ספרא's ולטעמיך. רב חסדא's נבלה case and רבי יוחנן בן נורי's שביתה case are laws of איסור, so they cannot disprove a distinction about money (claimants). It also follows that our dough, an איסור of תחומין, should be בטל, which leads to the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In איסור law, a minority is בטל no matter who owns it, so רב חסדא's and רבי יוחנן בן נורי's cases say nothing about claimants. In money law, an owner's property is not בטל, which is why the pebbles must be paid for. But our dough is about תחומין, an איסור, so the pebbles case does not help רבי אבא either, and the original question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritual prohibition (here, the תחום restriction)
Is nullified (loses its identity in a majority)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is saying the water and salt are בטל in the end. He is only saying that רב ספרא's proofs do not work. The גמרא will still give reasons why they are not בטל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic principle used across ש״ס. ביטול works on איסורים, not on someone's ownership of money.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: אביי responding to רב ספרא

phrases.english: Are you comparing a prohibition to money?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a rejection

phrases.english: A prohibition is nullified,
money is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי answers רב ספרא's ולטעמיך (steps 8-10) by distinguishing איסור from ממון. This also shows that the pebbles proof (step 6) does not apply to the איסור of תחומין.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב ספרא's counter-proofs from איסור cases (רב חסדא's נבלה and רבי יוחנן בן נורי's שביתה) against אביי's claimants distinction, and by extension the use of the pebbles case for תחומין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב ספרא compared איסור cases, where ביטול works regardless of ownership, to monetary law, where an owner's property is not בטל. The two systems run on different rules.

steps.title: So What Is the Real Reason?
steps.stepSummary: With the proofs rejected, the גמרא asks again: why aren't the water and salt בטל in the dough?
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next two steps. The גמרא is asking for a real reason, now that the money comparison has failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under normal איסור rules, the small amount of water and salt should be בטל. Yet the משנה says the dough is limited by the neighbor's תחום too. The גמרא needs an explanation that fits the rules of איסור.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reopens the original question after step 11 rejected the proofs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the borrowed water and salt are not בטל in the dough for תחומין.

steps.title: אביי: A Decree Because of Partnership Dough
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the rule is a rabbinic גזירה. Without it, people might confuse this case with a dough made in partnership, where every partner's תחום clearly applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a decree, lest she make a dough in partnership.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer. Strictly, the water and salt should be בטל, but the רבנן made a protective decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When several people make a dough together, each partner owns a real share. The dough can only go where all of them can go. A borrowed bit of salt and water looks similar, so חז״ל treated both cases the same to prevent mistakes. On this view the rule is only מדרבנן, not a true failure of ביטול.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a decree,
lest she make a dough in partnership.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rabbinic גזירה so that people do not confuse this case with a true partnership dough.

steps.title: רבא: Taste Is Never Nullified
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different reason. Spices like salt are added for their taste, and taste is never בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Spices are made for taste, and taste is not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second explanation that disagrees with אביי. He says the salt is truly not בטל, so no decree is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביטול works when a small ingredient gets lost in the mixture. Salt is added so that its taste will be noticed throughout the dough. Since its effect is felt, it can never be considered lost. So for רבא, the reason is built into the laws of ביטול, while for אביי it is a protective decree.
steps.whatToRemember: The water and salt are not בטל for two different reasons. אביי says it is a גזירה because of partnership dough. רבא says salt gives taste, and taste is never בטל.
steps.confusionAlert: The same word טַעְמָא means "reason" in step 12 but "taste" here. Read it from context.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's rule that a seasoning added for taste is not בטל appears widely in the laws of mixtures.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Spices are made for taste,
and taste is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the question of step 12, disagreeing with אביי in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Salt is added for taste, and taste is never בטל, so it is truly not nullified.
